title: Wendell and the Verdict
premise: When the coffin of town founder Aldous Verne is exhumed for a highway survey and found empty, night-shift taxi dispatcher Ivo Iversen discovers the last call Verne's widow made thirty years ago came through his company's old switchboard — a log only he can still read. Pulled in as a witness, Ivo traces a web of alibis woven by the founding families, uncovering that Verne faked his death to escape a crime he was about to confess to, and that his 'widow' has been hiding him alive ever since. As the trial of the man convicted in Verne's name approaches, Ivo must choose between duty to the court and loyalty to the fragile found family that took him in. In the end, Ivo testifies not to condemn but to reveal the truth: the real killer was Verne's business partner, now the town's presiding judge, and Verne died for real only weeks before the exhumation, leaving a confession that finally frees the innocent man.
about_author: Lena Ishikawa is a former small-town radio operator who spent a decade collecting the strange, tender stories that drift across late-night airwaves. She writes mysteries about quiet people who stumble into loud secrets, and lives with her partner and an opinionated cat named Dispatch.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Working his usual graveyard shift, Ivo takes the call from the cemetery caretaker reporting the opened, empty coffin of Aldous Verne. The town erupts by morning, and Ivo realizes he recognized the caretaker's voice — and that the man sounded terrified, not surprised. Emotional beat: unease; the ordinary night when everything tilts.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Static
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Digging through the taxi company's archived switchboard logs, Ivo finds a call from Verne's widow placed the night of the founder's supposed death — logged at an hour her official timeline says she was asleep. His boss warns him to leave it alone. Emotional beat: curiosity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Widow's Door
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo visits Marit Verne under the pretense of confirming an old fare record. She is gracious, sharp, and lying — he recognizes the cadence of someone rehearsed. But she also feeds him soup and asks about his life, the first kindness he's felt in years. Emotional beat: suspicion tangled with unexpected belonging.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Interviewing the founding families' aging heirs, Ivo collects four alibis so perfectly matched they must have been coordinated. Each heir mentions, unprompted, how much they owe the town's judge, Edmund Hale. Emotional beat: dread as patterns emerge.

chapters.title: The Man in the Passenger Seat
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A fare Ivo drives at 3 a.m. turns out to be Aldous Verne himself, alive, aged, and desperate. Verne begs Ivo to forget him, revealing he staged his death to flee something unspeakable. Emotional beat: shock and reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: What the Confession Cost
chapters.summary: Verne's POV (a letter interleaved with Ivo's investigation). Thirty years ago, Verne discovered his partner Hale had murdered a rival and let an innocent bookkeeper take the blame. Verne's cowardice — fleeing instead of testifying — haunts every line. Emotional beat: guilt across decades.

chapters.title: Subpoena
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The trial of the convicted bookkeeper's son, now accused of tampering with the grave, begins, and Ivo is subpoenaed. Judge Hale presides personally, watching Ivo with polite menace. Marit quietly tells Ivo where Verne is hiding. Emotional beat: pressure closing in from both duty and love.

chapters.title: The Switchboard Speaks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Reconstructing the full night from old tapes, Ivo proves Hale called the switchboard twice — once to arrange the fake death, once, years later, to check whether Verne's body would ever be dug up. He realizes Hale plans to make sure it never is. Emotional beat: clarity and fear.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the stand, Ivo plays the recovered tape over the judge's own courtroom speakers, then presents Verne's posthumous confession naming Hale as the murderer. The courtroom detonates; Hale orders Ivo silenced, and deputies arrest him instead. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage.

chapters.title: Night Shift, New Dawn
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Weeks later, the innocent man walks free, Marit opens Verne's estate into a community house, and Ivo — no longer alone — works his shift with the radio humming and friends dropping by. He visits Verne's true, modest grave. Emotional beat: belonging earned; love chosen over fear.
